replies.tweet: ok so I did my thesis on post-transit phenomenology and the six minutes thing is VERY documented it's called "transit grief" and it's caused by your temporal lobe briefly remembering a version of the journey that didn't happen. your brain mapped a path through normal space and when you skipped it, some part of you mourns the trip you never took. I cried in the Kepler-9 arrivals bay for seven minutes once and felt EMBARRASSED until I learned this was a thing
It's actually closer to 4 minutes 40 seconds. Not six. My wife has a stopwatch.

YES oh my god I thought I was insane. I used to think it was just me missing whoever I was leaving behind but I've done solo hops and it still happens. it's not about where you came from. it's something else. it's like grief for a place that doesn't have a name
